To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

four histidine auxotrophic mutants of B. japonicum were isolated by Tn5 random mutagenesis, that these mutants were defective in symbiotic nodulation, and that the symbiotic defect was complemented by the addition of histidine to the plant growth media.

(1) histidine is required for effective symbiosis between B. japonicum and soybeans; (2) two histidine auxotrophic mutants of B. japonicum, which do not require histidine for growth, do not form effective symbioses with soybean; (3) two histidine-auxotrophic mutants of Bradyrhizobia, which do not form effective nodules on soybean, are complemented to form effective symbiosi by histidine.
